sub_type_decided_by: Proof system named in the paper
technique: Groth16 via ZoKrates (ALT_BN128 curve, Ark/arkworks backend) (p.4-5)
what_the_proof_establishes: A T-step (up to 200) run of quantized UCB1 on a three-armed bandit was executed as encoded in one ZoKrates program, with data and parameters as private witness. The program covers rewards generated in-circuit by a seeded LCG with sliding-window averaging, average-reward and count updates, piecewise-linear ln, a 20-iteration Newton square root, and the argmax arm choice at every step.
largest_model_evaluated: UCB1 on a three-armed bandit run for 200 steps (state is per-arm averages and counts; no parameter count) (p.5-6)
prototype_proves_less: The use case specifies a statement over commitments to patient data and parameters (ϕ = (Cx, Ca, y), p.3), but the evaluated circuit is a synthetic three-armed bandit with in-circuit LCG rewards, and the implementation describes no commitments (p.4-6).
claim: zkUCB keeps training data and algorithm parameters confidential while making UCB decisions transparent and verifiable (p.1), securing 'precise algorithm output validation' (p.2).
datasets: none (synthetic three-armed bandit with expected rewards 0.9, 1.0 and 1.1)
proving_cost_largest_experiment: Full 200-step run, read approximately from bar charts (p.6-7): setup about 80 s, compile about 48 s, witness about 20 s, proof generation about 58 s, verification about 0.03-0.04 s. Reported 'proof size' is about 65 KB and grows linearly with steps; proving key about 1.7 GB, verifying key about 150 KB, witness about 150 MB. Hardware not stated.
trust_assumptions: trusted setup (Groth16 CRS with simulation trapdoor; in the AI-doctor use case the prover generates the CRS itself) (stated)

sub_type_decided_by: Proof system named in the paper

datasets: none (randomly generated synthetic data points, p.5 footnote 6)

trust_assumptions: trusted setup (model sponsor generates the keys and must delete the secret; an MPC setup is suggested as an alternative) (stated); committed training data is genuine (sensors with HSM-held keys are trusted and authenticated as sources of correct, untampered data) (stated)

sub_type_decided_by: Proof system named in the paper

largest_model_evaluated: Min-Char-RNN (one hidden layer, tanh/softmax), 12M parameters (p.10-11)
claim: SUMMER is an end-to-end zkPoT for RNN training that certifies forward, backward and parameter updates so the final parameters arise from honest BPTT on a committed dataset, with proof size and verification time independent of the number of iterations (p.1-2).
datasets: not stated (character-level Min-Char-RNN; training text not named)
proving_cost_largest_experiment: 12M-parameter Min-Char-RNN, T = 256 time steps: total prover 75.80 s per iteration amortized over a 100-iteration run (commitment 54.56 s, PBPTT 11.14 s), verifier 0.03 s and proof 164.59 KB for the whole run, peak memory 323.68 GB (Table 2, p.11-12); the abstract cites 70.1 s per iteration and a 165 KB proof verified in 20 ms.
trust_assumptions: random oracle (Fiat-Shamir) (stated); other: binding, extractable and hiding PCS and collision-resistant Merkle/hash construction (stated)

sub_type_decided_by: Proof system named in the paper
technique: Kaizen: GKR/sumcheck PoGD (zkCNN/Thaler sumchecks for linear layers, Virgo++ GKR for non-linear operations) with Orion polynomial commitments, MiMC-p²/p² hashing, and recursive composition (IVC) via a new aggregation scheme for multivariate polynomial commitments. Tree-based recursion (arity 12, depth 4) over F_{p²} with p = 2^61−1; built on the zkCNN and Virgo++ code bases (p.7, p.11).
what_the_proof_establishes: This holds for every executed mini-batch gradient-descent iteration, from the committed initial weights to the current committed weights. The batch items sit at positions fixed by a hard-coded per-epoch pseudorandom permutation and open against the dataset's Merkle root. The new weights equal one fixed-point GD step on that batch (forward pass, loss on the batch labels, backward pass, update W − η·G).
largest_model_evaluated: VGG-11 (channel-truncated), 10.1M parameters, batch size 16 (p.12)
prototype_proves_less: The evaluated implementation omits the zero-knowledge variants of sumcheck, Orion and aggregation (p.11), so the benchmarked prover proves correct training but is not zero-knowledge as the construction specifies.
claim: Kaizen lets a prover show that it correctly trained a committed model on a committed dataset by mini-batch gradient descent while revealing nothing else, with proof size and verifier time independent of the number of iterations (p.1; Theorem 4, p.11).
datasets: MNIST, CIFAR-10
proving_cost_largest_experiment: VGG-11, N = 16 (Table 2, p.12-13): amortized prover time 882.0 s per iteration (commitments 452.1 s, aggregation 142.1 s, recursion verifier 105.6 s, PoGD 182.2 s). The final proof is 1,627 KB and verification takes 0.130 s, both independent of the number of iterations. Peak prover memory 466.3 GB on an 8-CPU Xeon Platinum 8370 with 512 GB RAM. Building the CIFAR-10 dataset Merkle root takes 218 s.
trust_assumptions: random oracle (Fiat–Shamir) (stated); other: knowledge soundness of the commitment aggregation and IVC holds only for O(1) recursion depth, so the implementation bounds depth with tree-based recursion (arity 12, depth 4, at most 20,736 iterations) (stated)

trust_assumptions: random oracle (Fiat–Shamir) (stated); other: semi-honest verifier supplies the randomness (data subsets, Gaussian seed) instead of in-circuit randomness (stated); other: collision-resistant hash binds the private covariance Σ (stated); committed training data is genuine (where data are the prover's private input, as in Alg. 1 and the database mechanism, no data commitment is described) (unstated but needed)

sub_type_decided_by: Proof system named in the paper

technique: Interactive VOLE-based ZK (Wolverine/QuickSilver IT-MACs) in EMP-toolkit; SHA-256 commitment and digital signature for the shared seed; AES-128 PRG (p.4-7, p.9, p.14)

sub_type_decided_by: Proof system named in the paper
technique: QuickSilver (VOLE-based interactive ZK) via the emp-zk library of EMP-toolkit, Boolean circuits, 16 threads (p.10); backend-agnostic F_ZK abstraction (p.4); arithmetic-circuit sizes for zkSNARKs only estimated (p.13).

technique: Pairing-based additively homomorphic verification tags (Xu et al. [20]) with randomized batch verification, layered on Paillier threshold encryption (PCTD) and additive perturbation of the weights; Python implementation using pypbc, 256-bit security parameter (p.3-4, p.7, p.11).
what_the_proof_establishes: In every gradient-descent iteration of a linear SVM, the decrypted inner products c_i = sum_j x_ij*y_i*w_j are pairing-checked against published encodings g^(w_j) and h^(x_ij*y_i), and the gradient term c_j = eta*(eps*w_j - sum over {i: c_i<1} of x_ij*y_i), the new perturbed weights (old minus c_j) and the cost are checked against tags derived homomorphically from the data owners' and requester's tags; the checks are split between two non-colluding servers and the model requester.
